  • Method Details

    • period

      public TimelineProviderBase.TimelineBuilder period(int periodTicks)
      Sets the period of this timeline in ticks. The timeline repeats after that many ticks and all its keyframes and time markers must lie inside [0; periodTicks]. If this is not set, the timeline does not repeat and runs once over the entire lifetime of the world. Use TimelineProviderBase.DAY_TICKS for a timeline that repeats every overworld day.

    • track

      public <T> TimelineProviderBase.TimelineBuilder track(net.minecraft.world.attribute.EnvironmentAttribute<T> attribute, Consumer<net.minecraft.util.KeyframeTrack.Builder<T>> track)
      Adds a track that overrides the given attribute with the keyframed values. The keyframes are added through the given consumer. They must be sorted by their tick and at least one keyframe is required. The default easing is EasingType.LINEAR, use KeyframeTrack.Builder.setEasing(EasingType) to change it.

    • track

      public <T,A> TimelineProviderBase.TimelineBuilder track(net.minecraft.world.attribute.EnvironmentAttribute<T> attribute, net.minecraft.world.attribute.modifier.AttributeModifier<T,A> modifier, Consumer<net.minecraft.util.KeyframeTrack.Builder<A>> track)
      Adds a track that combines the current value of the given attribute with the keyframed values through the given modifier, for example ColorModifier.MULTIPLY_RGB to tint a color attribute or FloatModifier.MULTIPLY to scale a float attribute. The modifier must be allowed for the attributes type. The keyframes are added through the given consumer. They must be sorted by their tick and at least one keyframe is required. Note that the keyframe values are the arguments of the modifier, which need not have the same type as the attribute itself.

    • timeMarker

      public TimelineProviderBase.TimelineBuilder timeMarker(net.minecraft.resources.ResourceKey<net.minecraft.world.clock.ClockTimeMarker> marker, int ticks)
      Adds a time marker at the given tick to the clock of this timeline. The marker is not shown in the /time set command. A time marker key may only be defined once per clock, so a marker like ClockTimeMarkers.DAY can not be redefined for the overworld clock.

    • timeMarker

      public TimelineProviderBase.TimelineBuilder timeMarker(net.minecraft.resources.ResourceKey<net.minecraft.world.clock.ClockTimeMarker> marker, int ticks, boolean showInCommands)
      Adds a time marker at the given tick to the clock of this timeline. A time marker key may only be defined once per clock, so a marker like ClockTimeMarkers.DAY can not be redefined for the overworld clock.
      Parameters:
      showInCommands - whether the marker can be used as an argument to the /time set command.

    • build

      public net.minecraft.core.Holder<net.minecraft.world.timeline.Timeline> build()
      Builds the Timeline. This method returns an intrusive holder that must be properly added to the registry. RegistryProviderBase does this automatically if the result is stored in a public, non-static field inside the provider.
